content.value_statement: Complex software work needs clear agent roles, shared context, and reliable decisions. This skill guides Claude Flow Hive Mind sessions with queens, workers, consensus, and memory.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize and spawn Claude Flow Hive Mind sessions.
Describes strategic, tactical, and adaptive queen coordination patterns.
Shows how consensus, task distribution, and session management work.
Documents collective memory types, retrieval, associations, and checkpoints.
Provides examples for Claude Code, SPARC workflows, repository analysis, and reviews.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for memory, performance, and consensus issues.
limitations: Requires the external Claude Flow toolchain to run the documented commands.
Does not implement agents, memory storage, or consensus logic by itself.
Command examples may need adaptation for each repository and environment.
Reported benchmarks are documentation claims and should be validated locally.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-Agent Build
use_cases.description: Create a Hive Mind workflow with queen type, worker roles, consensus mode, and monitoring steps.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Code Review
use_cases.description: Use tactical worker roles to organize security, performance, test, and documentation review tasks.

use_cases.title: Manage Persistent Knowledge
use_cases.description: Design collective memory entries, associations, checkpoints, and retrieval patterns for repeated project work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Hive
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a Claude Flow Hive Mind session for this objective: [objective]. Recommend the queen type, worker roles, and first status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Coordination Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for roles and consensus.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Hive Mind plan for [project]. Compare strategic, tactical, and adaptive queens, then choose a consensus mode and worker count.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Hive
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hive Mind workflow to review [repository or pull request]. Include specialized reviewers, memory entries, checkpoints, and approval criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Long Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operations for performance and recovery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Hive Mind session plan for performance, memory pressure, consensus failure risk, and session recovery. Provide concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: Plan a Hive Mind session for building an authentication service.
output: Recommended queen: tactical, because implementation work needs close execution control.
Workers: backend, database, security, tester, reviewer, and documenter.
Consensus: weighted for architecture decisions, with checkpoints after design and implementation.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot slow Hive Mind task assignment.
output: Check pending tasks, idle workers, and queue utilization first.
Reduce worker mismatch by clarifying task labels and role capabilities.
Review memory size and cache settings before increasing concurrency.

output_examples.input: Design collective memory for API research.
output: Store durable architecture decisions as knowledge entries.
Use context entries for short-lived session details.
Create associations between API patterns, security choices, and test strategy.

best_practices: Pick the queen type from the work style before choosing worker count.
Use consensus only for decisions that need shared agreement or auditability.
Create checkpoints before major implementation, review, and deployment transitions.
anti_patterns: Do not spawn many workers before the objective and roles are clear.
Do not use Byzantine consensus for simple decisions that need speed.
Do not treat collective memory as a substitute for repository documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and operate Claude Flow Hive Mind workflows with coordinated agents, consensus, sessions, and shared memory.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents command patterns and workflow choices. Users remain responsible for running commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Which queen type should I choose?
faq.answer: Use strategic for planning, tactical for implementation, and adaptive for changing or optimization-heavy work.

faq.question: When should I use Byzantine consensus?
faq.answer: Use it for important decisions that need stronger agreement, such as release readiness or architecture approval.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for generating Claude Code task commands from Hive Mind plans.

faq.question: What should I verify before using it?
faq.answer: Verify the Claude Flow installation, repository permissions, command effects, and whether session memory may contain sensitive project data.
